newsitem.title: USA: Allstate property oper income up sharply.
newsitem.headline: Allstate property oper income up sharply.

text.p: Allstate Corp said operating income in its property-liability business rose 82.6 percent to $473 million in the first quarter due to increased earned premium, reduced claim volume as a result of better weather and lower catastophe losses.
Operating income a year ago was hurt by losses from severe winter weather, Allstate said.

Property-liability revenues rose 2.7 percent in the first quarter to $5.23 billion. Last year's property-liability revenues included revenue generated by commercial and reinsurance operations sold in the 1996 third quarter.
Personal lines written premium grew 6.2 percent to $4.55 billion as a result of increased standard and non-standard auto premiums.
"Allstate's continued growth in its core personal lines businesses, coupled with better weather and fewer accidents, made it the company's best quarter ever," Allstate Chairman Jerry Choate said.

"The company continued to see results from its strategic initiatives. Overall growth was particularly strong in light of the company's ongoing efforts to reduce catastrophe exposure in California and Florida," he said.
Realized capital gains were $159 million after-tax in the first quarter of 1997 compared with $76 million for the same period in 1996.
After-tax catastrophe losses for the period declined to $72 million from $151 million for the same period in 1996.
First quarter net income increased to $641 million in 1997 from $341 million a year ago.
